intros.perimeter: Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a flat shape. In practice you may be asked for the formula or to calculate it when side lengths are given (1–10).
intros.area: Area is the space inside a flat shape, measured in square units. Formula questions ask which expression to use; calculate questions plug in the dimensions.
intros.volume: Volume is the space inside a 3D shape, measured in cubic units. Square pyramid uses a square base; triangular pyramid is also called a tetrahedron when all faces are triangles; cone and cylinder answers may use π.

geometryLearn.piHint: Calculate answers use π forms (e.g. 10π), not decimals.
geometryLearn.fallbackExplanation: Use the formula with the labeled dimensions on the diagram.

perimeter.square: Perimeter is the distance around the outside. A square has four equal sides a, so add a + a + a + a, or 4 × a.
perimeter.rectangle: Walk all the way around: two sides of length a and two of length b. That is 2 × a + 2 × b, or 2 × (a + b).
perimeter.triangle: Add the lengths of all three sides a, b, and c. There is no shortcut unless two or more sides happen to be equal.
perimeter.circle: The distance around a circle is called the circumference. Multiply the diameter by π, or use 2 × π × r.
perimeter.rhombus: A rhombus has four equal sides a, like a tilted square. Perimeter is 4 × a.
perimeter.kite: A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides: two sides of length a meet at the top, and two longer sides of length b meet at the bottom. Perimeter is 2 × a + 2 × b.
perimeter.parallelogram: Opposite sides match in pairs: two sides of length a and two of length b. Perimeter is 2 × a + 2 × b, or 2 × (a + b).
perimeter.trapezoid: A trapezoid has four sides with one pair parallel: a and b are the top and bottom bases. The slanted legs are c and d. Perimeter = a + b + c + d.

area.square: Area counts square units that fit inside. A square with side a covers a rows of a squares, so area = a × a.
area.rectangle: Imagine rows of unit squares: a tells how many across, b how many down. Area = a × b.
area.triangle: A triangle is half of a matching rectangle with the same base a and height h. Area = ½ × a × h.
area.circle: Every circle with radius r covers π × r × r square units. That is why we write π × r².
area.rhombus: Diagonals d1 and d2 cross at right angles. Area equals half of d1 × d2.
area.kite: Like a rhombus, a kite has diagonals d1 and d2 that cross at right angles. Area = ½ × d1 × d2.
area.parallelogram: Use base a and the height h perpendicular to it (not the slanted side). Area = a × h.
area.trapezoid: Sides a and b are the parallel bases (top and bottom). Average them, then multiply by the height h between them: ½ × (a + b) × h.

volume.cube: A cube is like a 3D square. Multiply a × a × a to count cubic units inside.
volume.cuboid: A box shape: multiply a × b × c to fill it with unit cubes.
volume.pyramid: A square pyramid is one third of a box with the same square base a and height h: ⅓ × a² × h.
volume.cone: A cone is one third of a cylinder with the same circular base r and height h: ⅓ × π × r² × h.
volume.cylinder: Find the circular base area (π × r²), then stack it up through height h: π × r² × h.
volume.triangular_prism: First find the triangle face area (½ × a × h), then stretch it along length c.
volume.triangular_pyramid: Use triangle base a, triangle height b, and pyramid height h: one third of ½ × a × b × h.
